newsitem.title: USA: COMEX copper called to open slightly firmer.
newsitem.headline: COMEX copper called to open slightly firmer.

text.p: COMEX copper futures were seen opening slightly higher Wednesday, in line with LME copper prices, which found some support overnight following Tuesday's sharp sell off.
COMEX July copper was seen opening unchanged to up 0.50 cent a pound from Tuesday's close at 112.15 cents, after trading between 111.60 and 113.00 cents in overnight ACCESS trade.

LME copper prices were helped a little overnight by news the OK Tedi mine in Papua New Guinea would further scale back operations unless there was significant rain by the end of the week. OK Tedi produces around 60,000 tonnes of concentrates a month.

While the copper market was heading into the seasonally slow summer period, LME copper warehouse stocks had edged back up this week, and long liquidation by funds had driven the market sharply lower, the supply/demand fundamentals had not changed much, with the LME cash-to-three months spread still around $122.00 a tonne reflecting prompt market tightness, analysts argued.
LME copper stocks rose 875 tonnes to 123,125 tonnes in Wednesday's data, while COMEX copper stocks were up 300 short tons Tuesday to 49,930 short tons.
